faq: When did the November 2026 core update start?

Google started the November 2026 core update on 10 November 2026 at 10:06 Pacific time, according to its Search Status Dashboard. Google said the rollout may take up to two weeks to complete, which would put the latest finish on 24 November, three days before Black Friday.
How long should I wait before checking the core update's impact?

Google recommends confirming the update has finished, then waiting at least a full week before analysing your site in Search Console. If the rollout ends on 24 November, the first full week of data runs from 1 to 7 December 2026.
How do I separate the core update from Black Friday traffic?

Divide this year's change by last year's change over the same weeks. Take clicks for the week before the update and the week after it ends, then the same two weeks 364 days earlier. The result shows the update's effect with the usual seasonal rise taken out.
Should I change my content during the core update rollout?

Google advises against quick-fix changes during core updates and suggests not editing content that already performs well. Fix broken pages, indexing errors and speed problems straight away, but hold content rewrites until the rollout ends and the seasonally adjusted numbers show a real drop.

faq: What is the difference between MNQ and NQ?

MNQ, the Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100 future, is one tenth the size of NQ, the E-mini Nasdaq-100. MNQ is worth $2 per index point and NQ $20 per point. Both track the same index at the same prices, so a stop of a given number of points is the same on either; only the dollar risk per contract differs.
When should I switch from MNQ to NQ?

Switch once your risk budget per trade covers at least one NQ at your stop, which is the stop in points times $20, and one NQ round turn costs less than ten MNQ round turns at your broker. Below that budget, or when the NQ costs ten times the micro or more, stay in MNQ.
Can I trade NQ and MNQ at the same time?

Yes. Size the trade in micros, then replace every full block of ten MNQ with one NQ. The split carries the same risk as the all-micro size, because ten MNQ equal one NQ point for point, and you pay commission on fewer contracts. Check your prop firm's contract caps before mixing.
How much did MNQ volume grow in October 2026?

CME Group reported Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures average daily volume of 2.9 million contracts in October 2026, up 74% year on year. All Micro E-mini equity index futures and options averaged 4.4 million contracts a day, half of CME's equity index volume.

faq: Which MCP servers are deprecated?

On 5 November 2026 the npm registry marked 11 official @modelcontextprotocol packages as deprecated, including server-github, server-puppeteer, server-postgres, server-slack and server-gdrive. The Python servers mcp-server-sqlite and mcp-server-sentry are archived too. Filesystem, Memory, Sequential Thinking, Everything, Git, Fetch and Time remain active.
What is MCPhantom?

MCPhantom is the name security firm Glow gave, in November 2026, to AI coding agents installing deprecated MCP servers from their training data. In 98% of the sessions it studied, the agent chose the outdated package itself. Glow found four high-severity flaws in those servers that will not be patched.
How do I check if an MCP server package is deprecated?

Run npm view followed by the package name and the word deprecated, for example npm view @modelcontextprotocol/server-github deprecated. The registry prints the deprecation notice if there is one and nothing if the package is current. For Python servers, check the last release date on PyPI and the project's repository.
What should replace the deprecated GitHub MCP server?

GitHub maintains its own MCP server in the github/github-mcp-server repository, available as a remote server or the ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server container. Switch to it, give it a token scoped to the repositories the agent needs, and keep that token in an environment variable rather than the config file.

faq: Was there a Google algorithm update in October 2026?

Not a confirmed one, as of 1 November 2026. Google's last confirmed change was the September 2026 spam update, which ran from 24 September to 8 October. Rank trackers reported unconfirmed volatility on 16, 20 to 21, 24 and 27 October, and Google's Search Status Dashboard lists no incident since.
How do I tell if a ranking drop is an algorithm update or a site problem?

Check Search Console in order. Manual actions or security issues explain a drop on their own. If one folder holds most of the lost clicks, suspect a template or indexing change. If top queries lost three or more places and Crawl stats and Page indexing look clean, the evidence points to an algorithmic cause.
Why did my clicks drop when impressions stayed the same?

Clicks equal impressions times CTR, so steady impressions mean your click-through rate fell. Google still shows your pages, but fewer people choose them, often because an AI Overview, video block or rich result now sits above you. Rewrite titles and snippets for the queries that lost the most clicks.
How long should I wait after a Google ranking drop before changing pages?

Google says some changes take effect in a few days and others take several months, and suggests waiting a few weeks before analysing the site in Search Console again. Log the date and numbers now, then compare the same windows two weeks after the volatility settles.

toc: How many variations can you afford?
Build the checks into the engine
faq: What should a backtest checklist include?

Seven tests, run in order: no future data (truncation test), costs that survive doubled slippage, enough trades for a t-stat of 2, a deflated Sharpe ratio of 95% after counting every variation, out-of-sample Sharpe at least half of in-sample, a parameter plateau, and profit in both volatility regimes without the best 1% of trades.
How many trades do you need for a valid backtest?

Enough for the t-stat of your average net trade to reach 2: trades needed = (2 × standard deviation per trade ÷ average net trade) squared. With a $15.20 average and $118 standard deviation, that is about 241 trades. A wider spread or a thinner edge needs more.
What is the deflated Sharpe ratio?

The deflated Sharpe ratio, from Bailey and López de Prado (2014), is the probability that a strategy's Sharpe ratio beats the best result luck would produce across all the variations you tested. After 240 variations on 4 years of data, luck alone gives an expected best annual Sharpe of about 1.41.
What is a good out-of-sample Sharpe compared with in-sample?

A common rule of thumb, stated in TradeStation's walk-forward optimiser documentation for annualised returns, is 50% or more of the in-sample figure. Applied to Sharpe, an in-sample 1.60 needs at least 0.80 on unseen data. Below that, most of the in-sample result likely came from fitting.

posts.meta: Bulenox cut Momentum drawdowns and Lucid moved to a 40% consistency rule. Use the formula, worked MNQ examples and a free calculator to re-size.
faq: What is the new Bulenox Momentum drawdown?

Bulenox lowered Momentum drawdowns in October 2026: the 50K went from $2,250 to $2,000, the 100K from $4,000 to $3,000 and the 150K from $5,500 to $4,500. The cut applies to both the trailing and end-of-day options. Daily loss limits and contract caps did not change.
How do I calculate position size on a prop firm account?

Divide your room to the failure level by the loss one contract takes across the losing streak you want to survive: room ÷ (stop in points × point value × losses). With $3,000 of room, a 20-point MNQ stop ($2 per point) and 5 losses, that is $3,000 ÷ $200 = 15 contracts.
What is Lucid's 40% consistency rule?

On LucidFlex evaluations your best single day can be at most 40% of your total profit, down from 50%; the 50% level is now a paid add-on. It means you need at least three winning days, and on a 50K with a $3,000 target any day above $1,200 raises the profit you need to pass.
Is Lucid's 50% consistency add-on worth paying for?

Work out your best-day share: your largest day divided by net profit over your last 20 trading days. Under 40%, the add-on buys nothing. Between 40% and 50%, price it against the extra days you would trade. Over 50%, a daily stop-win fixes the problem better than the add-on.

faq: What did Microsoft say about AI agents being insiders?

On 19 October 2026, Microsoft Security argued that companies should treat AI agents as insiders rather than trusted tools. Its guidance: give each agent its own identity, start it with no permissions, grant access only for the current task and require verified human approval for higher-impact actions.
How do I apply least privilege to an AI agent?

List every tool the agent can call and give it a separate API key or service account. Grant read and reversible draft access only, make credentials expire when the task ends, and keep payment, deletion and credential permissions on a key the agent never holds.
Which AI agent actions should need human approval?

Anything that leaves your company or can't be undone within about five minutes: customer emails, publishing, changes customers can see, and edits to financial records. Refunds, payments, deleting records and changing permissions shouldn't be on the agent's key at all.
What is OWASP Excessive Agency?

Excessive Agency is entry LLM06 in OWASP's 2025 Top 10 for LLM applications. It covers damage caused when an AI system has functions it doesn't need, more permissions than its task requires, or the autonomy to take high-impact actions without approval.
